name: Ottolenghi's Burrata with Grilled Grapes & Basil
description: Creamy burrata with blistered grapes in a sherry vinegar marinade, topped with toasted fennel

equipment.notes: 6-8 skewers - if using wooden, soak in water 30 minutes first
Cast iron preferred for high heat

equipment.alternative: Crush fennel seeds with bottom of pan or knife

equipment.notes: 6 individual plates or one large platter

ingredients.notes: Valdespino or other quality sherry vinegar
Purple basil is beautiful here but regular works

prep_steps.instruction: Set up your staging area: get out a medium bowl for marinating, your skewers, and measuring spoons. If using wooden skewers, soak them in water now.
prep_steps.notes: Soaking wooden skewers prevents them from burning

prep_steps.instruction: Pull grapes off the vine and place in the medium bowl
prep_steps.notes: Discard any soft or split grapes

prep_steps.instruction: Crush the garlic clove with the flat side of your knife (peel will come off easily after crushing)
prep_steps.notes: Add directly to bowl with grapes

prep_steps.instruction: Toast fennel seeds in dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Transfer to mortar and lightly crush (or crush with knife/pan bottom). Measure out 1 teaspoon for marinade, reserve 1/2 teaspoon for garnish.
prep_steps.notes: Don't over-crush - you want texture, not powder

prep_steps.instruction: Add to the bowl with grapes: sherry vinegar, olive oil, brown sugar, 1 teaspoon of the toasted fennel seeds, 1/4 teaspoon flaked salt, and plenty of black pepper. Mix well.
Cover and marinate grapes for at least 1 hour at room temperature, or up to 1 day in the refrigerator
prep_steps.notes: The longer the better - overnight is great. Reserve the marinade!

prep_steps.instruction: Thread 5-6 marinated grapes onto each skewer. Keep the marinade - you'll need it for serving.
prep_steps.notes: Don't pack grapes too tightly - leave small gaps

prep_steps.instruction: Take burrata out of refrigerator 20 minutes before serving to bring to room temperature
prep_steps.notes: Cold burrata doesn't have the same creamy texture

cook_steps.instruction: Heat grill pan over high heat until very hot. Make sure kitchen is well ventilated - this will smoke.

cues.visual: Pan is slightly smoking, a drop of water evaporates instantly

cook_steps.warnings: Turn on exhaust fan - grilling grapes creates smoke

cook_steps.instruction: Add grape skewers to hot grill pan in batches (don't overcrowd). Grill for 2-3 minutes total, turning once after about 1.5 minutes.

cues.visual: Grapes are blistered and have light char marks, skins splitting slightly

cook_steps.warnings: Don't overcook - grapes should still hold their shape

cook_steps.instruction: Remove skewers from heat and set aside briefly while you plate

finishing.instructions: Tear each ball of burrata in half and place one half on each plate (or arrange on platter). Lean 2 grape skewers against each portion of burrata. Spoon about 1 1/2 teaspoons of the reserved marinade over each cheese portion. Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 teaspoon crushed fennel seeds over all portions. Garnish each plate with a sprig of basil. Serve immediately while grapes are still warm.
finishing.make_ahead: Grapes can marinate up to 1 day ahead. Grill just before serving. Burrata should be fresh.
finishing.storage: This dish doesn't keep well - serve immediately. Leftover marinade can be used as salad dressing.

notes: The contrast of warm blistered grapes against cool creamy burrata is essential
Don't skip marinating time - it develops the flavor
Valdespino sherry vinegar is specified but any quality sherry vinegar works
Purple basil makes it stunning but green basil tastes the same
Can be scaled up easily for a crowd - use a large platter for presentation
